talk_track:
I've spent the last few years moving work that lived in people's hands into AI systems that held up under real load — AI agents for incident detection and on-call response at Tricentis, and a services-to-SaaS platform transition at Avathon before that. Your open Head of ERP Implementations role asks that person to "recruit and lead a team of 15+ CX Leads and Customer Support specialists, and will continue to hire and scale the team quickly." Here is the read worth having whether or not we ever speak: for a product sold on the finance team of one, implementation is the last place where cost-to-serve still scales one-for-one with customers, and that ratio is what a Series B diligence process prices. The same posting asks the hire to "establish and evolve implementation methodologies, processes, and operational standards" — written once with agents in mind, that document is the spec for the system that replaces most of the 15; written twice, it becomes a services org bolted to a software company. Which parts of go-live do you think stay permanently human?

— Daniel
